comparisons.peer_topic: Consumer Lending risk-adjusted margin and purchase volumes
comparisons.peer_summary: Total risk-adjusted margin decreased 85 bps driven by higher net credit losses, while total credit card and debit card purchase volumes increased to $368.9 billion and $557.0 billion respectively, reflecting higher consumer spending.
comparisons.comparison: Bank of America explicitly links its margin compression in 2024 to the same underlying factor affecting Citigroup: higher net credit losses. While Citigroup reported a 40% increase in net credit losses to $9.0 billion, Bank of America stated that its total risk-adjusted margin decreased by 85 basis points 'primarily driven by higher net credit losses.' Both disclosures illustrate the industry-wide impact of rising consumer credit losses on profitability and margin metrics in 2024, despite differing absolute provision amounts.

sentences.text: Net credit losses of $9.0 billion increased 40% from the prior year.
Total risk-adjusted margin decreased 85 bps primarily driven by higher net credit losses, partially offset by higher net interest margin and higher net fee income.

comparisons.peer_summary: Provision for credit losses increased to $1.54 billion in 2024 from $1.14 billion in 2023, primarily driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Citigroup report significant increases in their credit loss provisions in 2024 driven primarily by credit card portfolio performance. Goldman Sachs reported a provision for credit losses of $1.54 billion, an increase from $1.14 billion in 2023, which it explicitly attributed to net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio. Similarly, Citigroup reported a massive increase in net credit losses to $9.0 billion, with the consumer segment (dominated by Branded Cards) rising 39% to $8.6 billion. While Citigroup's total credit losses are substantially larger in absolute terms due to its scale, both peers identify the credit card segment as the primary driver of deteriorating credit quality and increased provisions/losses in 2024.

sentences.text: Consumer net credit losses of $8.6 billion increased 39%, largely reflecting the continued rise in net credit loss rates in Branded Cards and Retail Services.
Provisions for 2024 reflected net provisions related to the credit card portfolio (primarily driven by net charge-offs).

comparisons.peer_topic: Provision for Credit Losses and Allowance Metrics
comparisons.peer_summary: The provision for credit losses was $10.7 billion (up from $9.3 billion prior year), reflecting $8.6 billion in net charge-offs driven by Card Services and a $2.0 billion net addition to the allowance, which totaled $26.9 billion at year-end.
comparisons.comparison: JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup both highlight that their increased credit loss provisions and net charge-offs in 2024 were significantly driven by their Card Services (consumer credit card) businesses. JPMorgan reported a $10.7 billion provision for credit losses, noting that $8.6 billion in net charge-offs were 'driven by Card Services.' Citigroup reported $9.0 billion in total net credit losses, with $8.6 billion attributed to the consumer segment, which is largely composed of its Branded Cards business. Both disclosures underscore consumer credit cards as the central risk area and financial driver for the year's credit loss metrics.

sentences.text: Consumer net credit losses of $8.6 billion increased 39%, largely reflecting the continued rise in net credit loss rates in Branded Cards and Retail Services.

• The provision for credit losses was $10.7 billion, reflecting $8.6 billion of net charge-offs and a net addition to the allowance for credit losses of $2.0 billion. Net charge-offs increased by $2.4 billion, driven by Card Services, reflecting the seasoning of vintages originated in recent years, credit normalization, and balance growth. The net addition to the allowance for credit losses included a net addition of $2.1 billion in consumer, driven by Card Services, and a net reduction of $19 million in wholesale.
